newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran quakes kill 72, strong aftershock jolts area.
newsitem.headline: Iran quakes kill 72, strong aftershock jolts area.

text.p: A powerful aftershock on Wednesday jolted mountainous northeastern Iran as the toll from two earlier earthquakes rose to 72 dead and 200 injured, state-run Tehran radio said.

It said the aftershock, measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale, occured at 11:24 a.m. (0754 GMT). It was centered near Bojnurd, about 580 km (360 miles) northeast of Tehran -- the same area which was the epicentre of two quakes measuring 5.4 and 6.1 on Tuesday.
In Bojnurd and nearby Shirvan, 72 people were reported killed and 200 people injured as rescue work continued in 73 villages which were levelled or heavily damaged, the radio said.
But rescue teams had been unable to reach 21 villages because the quakes had cut connecting roads, it added.
The Bojnurd area, near the border with Turkmenistan, has an estimated population of 14,000 people.
The head of the geophysics institute at the region's Mashhad University said it had registered more than 100 aftershocks in nine hours on Tuesday, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
The radio said emergency supplies including tents, blankets, foodstuffs, clothing and heaters were being sent by land and air to the stricken rural region.
It said on Tuesday relief efforts were hampered by nightfall and snow which had cut rural roads.

Iranian oil output and export operations were unaffected by the quakes which hit an area over 1,000 km (625 miles) from the main oil province of Khuzestan in the southwest. Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter behind Saudi Arabia and Norway, Iranian and foreign oil industry sources said.
Tremors of force six can cause widespread damage and those of force five are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in a densely populated area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
